Two infrastructure tiers

Standard Infrastructure · Non-HA

$3,000–$6,000

One-time professional services · USD

For smaller businesses, internal applications, and workloads that can tolerate occasional downtime.

  • Single VPS or physical host, with custom configurations available

  • Single-instance databases
  • Monitoring, alerts, TLS and access controls

High Availability Infrastructure · HA

$8,000–$15,000+

One-time professional services · USD

For business-critical workloads that need redundancy designed around agreed recovery goals.

  • Managed Kubernetes with an HA control plane, or a custom self-managed HA architecture
  • Multiple workers, replicated workloads and multi-node failover where supported
  • CloudNativePG for PostgreSQL, with Galera or suitable clustering for MariaDB
  • Redundant routing and persistent storage designed per workload
  • GitOps, monitoring, alerting and incident response runbooks
  • Offsite backups, restoration tests and AI-assisted troubleshooting

Architecture and operations

Version-controlled changes

I use infrastructure as code to provision environments from the same configuration. With GitOps or a comparable review process, administrators can see changes and roll them back.

Identity and networking

I configure centralized authentication for applications that support it. We agree on who can reach each service and how to apply TLS, network segmentation, and access policies.

Monitoring and recovery

I set up metrics and alerts for key services. I configure offsite backups, document the restore procedure, and test it against the retention and recovery goals.

Documentation and administrator training

I hand over the architecture diagrams and deployment repositories. Your administrators receive operating and troubleshooting runbooks, instructions for backups, restores, and upgrades, and hands-on training.

  1. Monitoring detects a potential issue.
  2. AI reads permitted metrics, logs and runbooks.
  3. AI proposes a diagnosis or change.
  4. An administrator reviews and approves the action.
  5. The deployment workflow applies the approved change.
  6. The team monitors and documents the outcome.

Optional AI-searchable documentation and diagnostics can use a self-hosted model where practical. Production actions require least-privilege access, human approval and an auditable change record.

Frequently asked questions

What do I own in the cloud?

You control your cloud account, data, configuration, and workloads. The cloud provider owns the physical equipment that runs your rented services.

Does Kubernetes make an application highly available?

Availability depends on the application’s replication behavior, network and ingress, database failover, shared storage and failure domains. I assess and test each component as part of the availability design.

Can my team operate the system after delivery?

I train your administrators and give them runbooks to operate the system. You can arrange extra training or ongoing support.
